title: Record-Breaking Splashes and Surprise Comebacks at the Sette Colli Trophy!
summary: Imagine you're about to race, and then—whoops!—you get disqualified. That's what happened to Italian swimmer Sara Curtis this morning. But she didn't give up. She got the decision overturned (changed) and came back tonight to do something amazing. She blasted through the water in the women's 50 backstroke, touching the wall in 27.07 seconds. That's a new European Record! The old record was 27.10, set way back in 2021. Curtis was so fast, she's now the second-fastest in the world this year. Only American Katharine Berkoff has gone faster. The crowd in Rome went wild! There were other surprises too. Some big stars like Adam Peaty and Thomas Ceccon didn't even make the 'A' final in their events. That left room for new faces to shine. In the men's 400 freestyle, Italian Marco De Tullio led from the very first lap and won by almost two seconds. His brother Luca also swam fast, taking second in the morning heats. The meet is full of showdowns—like Gretchen Walsh vs. Sarah Sjostrom in the 50 fly, racing each other for the first time since 2023. And in the men's 50 breaststroke, four swimmers from different countries are all within a blink of each other. It's going to be a splashing good weekend!
why_it_matters: Just like Sara Curtis didn't give up after being disqualified, you can bounce back from a bad day at school or a tough sports practice.

background_read: The Sette Colli Trophy is a famous swimming meet held every summer in Rome, Italy. It draws top swimmers from Europe and around the world.
Adam Peaty (a British swimmer who has won Olympic gold medals) and Thomas Ceccon (an Italian Olympic champion) are usually big favorites, so missing the final was a huge surprise.
Article_Structure: WHO: Italian swimmer Sara Curtis, along with Marco De Tullio, Adam Peaty, Thomas Ceccon, and other international swimmers.
WHAT: A series of surprising results and a record-breaking performance at the Sette Colli Trophy swimming meet.
WHERE: The swimming pool in Rome, Italy, where the crowd went wild.
WHY: Because big stars fell short in heats, new faces got a chance to shine, and Sara Curtis overcame a morning disqualification to set a European record.
